picks.title: Ludo.ai brings AI game asset creation into the developer terminal with new CLI
picks.excerpt: Ludo.ai released the Ludo CLI, letting developers and coding agents such as Claude Code generate sprites, animations, images, 3D models, video and audio for games directly from the terminal; it is available on Pro and Studio plans.
picks.rationale: Concrete new tool release: agent-callable CLI for sprites, animation, 3D and audio, directly changes how game artists and devs generate assets.

picks.title: Steam Fans Are Begging for a No-AI Filter as Steam Next Fest Is Filled With Slop
picks.excerpt: Steam Next Fest opened with more than 8,000 demos, and players are calling on Valve to add a filter that hides games disclosing generative AI as low-effort AI-made entries flood the event.
picks.rationale: Fresh platform-level event (October Next Fest, 8,000+ demos) shaping discoverability and AI-disclosure stakes for every Steam developer.

picks.title: The Finals adding real-time AI commentary in new update that'll call out people's usernames
picks.excerpt: Embark Studios is rolling out real-time AI commentary in The Finals: announcers Scott and June will now call out individual players' usernames during play-by-play when they make big plays.
picks.rationale: Shipping in-game AI feature in a live AAA shooter: real-time personalized announcer audio, a concrete design reference for AI dialogue.

picks.title: UKIE partners with Sheridans on AI Compliance and Accreditation Service to guide UK studios in using AI lawfully and responsibly
picks.excerpt: UK trade body Ukie and law firm Sheridans launched an AI Compliance and Accreditation Service: a four-step process that ends in an AI Certification Mark studios can show in pitches and funding rounds.
picks.rationale: New industry-body service launch with a certification mark studios can use in pitches; practical compliance path, not commentary.

picks.title: Japanese acting union fights back against AI-generated voice use, proposing strict new guidelines, especially regarding the use of a deceased actor's voice
picks.excerpt: Japanese actors are trying to control the spread of AI-generated voices by establishing strict rules around use and total bans on imitating dead people.
picks.rationale: New union guideline proposal (incl. ban on deceased-actor voice imitation) that affects voice pipelines for Japanese game production.
